title: The Secret Signal
markdown:
Click. Beep-beep. Click. Beep-beep. Ines was already at the radio shack when the secret heartbeat arrived, seven on the dot. Pink and gold streaked the glass. Dock, her whippet, thumped his tail against a crate of coiled cable. The air smelled of ozone and dew.

For weeks the same pattern had pinged the school radio, then gone silent. Ines had tweaked antennae until her fingers tingled. Town chatter, weather, the usual clutter — none of it matched this. “Someone is out there, Dock.” The beeps pulsed stronger tonight. Dock growled, ears perked. “Not from town. Closer. Different.”

She grabbed a sketchpad and tried to triangulate from the shack roof. The needles disagreed. The signal hopped, as if it did not care for her tidy circles. Crisis one: she could hear it and still not place it. Dock nudged her hand, then trotted to the door. Outside, then. She grinned. “You brilliant dog.”

They slipped into the cool. Dock became a streak of grey lightning across the grass. Ines followed, heart thumping. The faint pulse seemed to tug.

He veered toward the overgrown grounds behind the abandoned sports fields. Forgotten territory. Brambles thickened. Dock stopped, whined, pawed thorns. Crisis two: the trail died in a tangle that wanted blood for passage. Ines knelt, pushed vines aside, and found a heavy metal door. A storm shelter, ancient, rusted. Powered? Emitting? Ridiculous. She almost turned back for a teacher, a key, a better plan.

The handle groaned. Then, with a surprising click, it gave. Faint light spilled. The signal pulsed strongest here. Inside, wires snaked the walls to a humming generator. A compact transmitter beat those same beeps. Crisis three, and the worst: someone had built a hidden station on school ground, and she was standing in it alone except for a dog, with no idea whether the next sound would be a person coming back.

Dock wagged, nudged the generator, then looked at her. Ines breathed. The code was cracked. The wonder had only started.

She did not wind the mystery down. She logged the frequency in her head, shut the door on the hum, and stepped into the blazing pre-dawn. “Today,” she told Dock, determined and already moving, “is going to be amazing.” They raced toward the awakening town, ready for whatever came next.
